clue.text: I'm not sure try's given as a result

parts.note: the hesitant noise someone makes when unsure
to have a go is to have a try

explanation.surface: Someone hesitantly concludes that an attempt has led to some outcome.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe-s on 'try's' is read as 'is': ER plus GO is given for the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ergo is the Latin-derived word meaning therefore, used to introduce a logical consequence.

clue.text: Main bottom in butt, behind

parts.note: the main is an old poetic name for the open ocean

indicators.note: the bottom of a word written downwards is its final letter, so only that end is kept

parts.note: the closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A sniggering line about the rear end, with butt and behind both pointing to the same place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Main' looks like an adjective meaning chief, but here it is the noun for the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Seat is a polite word for the buttocks, just as behind is, both naming the part one sits on.

clue.text: Plaster coming off initially after upping of austerity measures

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending a word up the column means writing it from bottom to top

parts.note: government spending cuts are the measures of austerity

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each word it governs

parts.note: the first letter of each of these two words

explanation.surface: Plaster flaking off a building once austerity cuts are increased, as maintenance budgets shrink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'After' tells you the two first letters go behind the turned-round word.
explanation.definitionFit: Stucco is a fine plaster or render used to coat and decorate walls and facades.

clue.text: Pile I fed to males

indicators.note: something fed to another goes inside it, so one piece is placed within the other

parts.note: two male words side by side: a man and a son
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone boasts of feeding a heap of food to a group of men.
explanation.walkthrough: The plural 'males' supplies two separate male words, MAN and SON, and the I goes between them.
explanation.definitionFit: A pile is a large imposing house, as in a stately pile, so a mansion is an example.

clue.text: Ambitious foursome you''ll find on the periphery from 17, did you say?

indicators.note: asking whether you said something means attending to how the words are pronounced

parts.words: foursome you''ll find on the periphery from 17
parts.note: a small cell of agents, such as a group of four, operating on the margins besides (17) normal society

explanation.surface: A foursome hovering at the edge of things, asked if they have ambitions.
explanation.walkthrough: Spoken aloud the answer is 'a spy ring'. How 'on the periphery from 17' (BESIDES) describes that ring is not clear; it may allude to the Cambridge spies.
explanation.definitionFit: An aspiring person is hoping and striving to achieve something, which is what being ambitious means.

clue.text: Blends dispensed from some optics

indicators.note: letters dispensed are let out and scattered, so they come out in a different order

parts.note: the ten letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Mixed drinks poured from the optics behind a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: Optics are the upside-down spirit dispensers mounted behind a British bar, which is why blends sound like whiskies here.
explanation.definitionFit: Composites are materials or things made by combining several components, which is what blends are.

clue.text: Drive two into the water

indicators.note: one thing going into another ends up enclosed inside it

parts.note: a lido is an open-air swimming pool or bathing place
the prefix meaning two, as in bicycle

explanation.surface: An instruction to steer a pair of vehicles into a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drive' looks like a verb about a car; it is the noun for an inner urge. A lido is a public outdoor pool, common in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Libido is sexual desire, often called the sex drive, so drive in that sense is a synonym.

clue.text: Penning first in trilogy, author needing a drink

indicators.note: penning something means writing it in or enclosing it, so one piece holds another

parts.note: Graham Greene, the English novelist

indicators.note: the first in a word is its opening letter only

parts.note: opening letter of this word
taken as written

explanation.surface: A novelist writing the first book of a trilogy who needs a drink to keep going.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' fits the writer of the surface, but here it is the author's name that pens the letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Green tea is an unfermented tea brewed as a drink, so it is a specific example of a beverage.

clue.text: Something to draw on right-hand side of page, so it could be?

indicators.note: what letters could be, if reshuffled, is a different arrangement of them
the right-hand half of a written word is its last letters

parts.note: the right half of the four-letter word
taken as written for rearranging

explanation.surface: An artist wondering whether the right-hand side of the page might do as a place to sketch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Draw on' suggests pencil and paper; it means to puff on, as one draws on a cigar.
explanation.definitionFit: A stogie is a long cheap cigar, and smokers draw on a cigar by inhaling through it.

clue.text: Search close to over, with licence to kill time

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter, which is all that is used

parts.note: closing letter of this word
James Bond's 00 prefix, the double-O, marks an agent licensed to kill
T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A spy thriller: the search nears its end, with a licence to kill time.
explanation.walkthrough: The zeros of 007 are read as the letters O O.
explanation.definitionFit: To root, or root around, is to search by rummaging through things, as a pig roots for food.

clue.text: Number going into two, neatly

indicators.note: something going into words sits inside them, so the letters are found within

parts.note: the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A sum where one figure divides neatly into another.
explanation.walkthrough: Arithmetic tempts: no division is needed, the letters are sitting across the comma.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the first of the cardinal numbers, the figure for a single unit.

clue.text: Exercise beyond Shakespearean lieutenant, one with a vain queen

parts.note: Cassio is Othello's lieutenant
physical education
the Roman numeral for one
taken as written

explanation.surface: A workout scene from a production of Othello, the officer joined by a conceited monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beyond' places the exercise after the lieutenant.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth Cassiopeia, queen of Ethiopia, boasted that she was more beautiful than the sea nymphs, which is vanity.

clue.text: Scientific body in fluid ounces

indicators.note: fluid things have no fixed shape, so these letters can flow into another order

parts.note: the six letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Lab scientists measuring their liquids in fluid ounces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fluid ounces' reads as a single unit of measure; split it, and the first word works on the second.
explanation.definitionFit: UNESCO is the United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organization, an international organization dealing with science among other fields.

clue.text: Born in the jungle, only fundamental characters?

indicators.note: the fundament is the bottom, so only the letters at the bottom end of each word count

parts.note: the final letter of each of these three words

explanation.surface: A creature born and raised in the wild, knowing only the basics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fundamental' sounds like basic, but the fundament is the backside, so the clue wants the tail of each word.
explanation.definitionFit: Née, French for born, introduces a woman's maiden name, as in Mrs Smith née Jones.

clue.text: Marine animal saw a vehicle, say, flooded with last of water

indicators.note: something flooded with water has it inside, so one piece is filled with another
say tells you to go by the sound of the words spoken

parts.note: saw means spied and a taxi is a cab; run together the phrase is said like the letters given

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter alone

parts.note: closing letter of this word

explanation.surface: A sea creature spots a car that then floods with seawater.
explanation.walkthrough: The comma before 'say' looks like grammar, but 'say' works on the phrase before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider crab is a long-legged crab of the sea floor, so it is a kind of marine animal.

clue.text: So scratching head with task — forgotten something?

indicators.note: scratching out the head of a word strikes off its first letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its head
a mission is an assigned task

explanation.surface: Someone scratching their head over a job, sure they have forgotten something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Scratching head' paints puzzlement but means chopping the first letter off the word before it.
explanation.definitionFit: An omission is a thing left out or overlooked, so it is something forgotten; the question mark flags the noun definition.

clue.text: Less familiar tunes including Beethoven's Second, moreover

indicators.note: something including another holds it within itself

parts.note: B-sides are the lesser tracks on the reverse of a single

indicators.note: the second of a word is its letter in position two

parts.note: the letter after the B of the composer's name

explanation.surface: An album of obscure numbers that also includes Beethoven's Second Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beethoven's Second' looks like a symphony; it is the second letter of his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Besides and moreover are both sentence adverbs used to add a further point to an argument.

clue.text: Label written up, amended date issued

indicators.note: in a down clue, writing a word up the column puts it bottom to top

parts.note: to label something is to name it, and a name is a label

indicators.note: amended letters are altered, here rearranged into a new order

parts.note: the four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Office procedure: a label is written out and a corrected date is issued.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issued' sits at the end looking like part of the story; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Emanated means came forth or flowed out from a source, which is what issued means as an intransitive verb.

clue.text: Ultimately, race won with burst, in journey of self love

indicators.note: ultimately points to what comes at the very end, the final letter

parts.note: final letter of this word
to have won something is to have got it
a rip is a burst or tear

explanation.surface: A runner wins with a final burst of speed and basks in self-admiration.
explanation.definitionFit: An ego trip is an action undertaken to boost one's own self-importance; the definition puns on trip as journey.

clue.text: Princess sounding like a duck

indicators.note: sounding like asks for a word pronounced the same as another

parts.note: the eider is a sea duck, the source of eiderdown

explanation.surface: A princess whose voice is compared to a quack.
explanation.walkthrough: In non-rhotic British speech the name and the duck are said the same way.
explanation.definitionFit: Princess Ida is the title heroine of the Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, so she is a well-known princess.

clue.text: Style of delivery from member with political bias

parts.note: a limb is a member of the body
spin is the slanted presentation of news by politicians

explanation.surface: A politician's delivery style, marked by partisan bias.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a leg-spinner bowls wrist spin that turns from leg to off; delivery is the bowler's ball, not a speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Leg spin is a type of bowling in cricket, and each ball bowled is called a delivery.

clue.text: Bear hugs real hairy bear!

indicators.note: hairy means wild and alarming, so these letters are thrown into disorder
one thing hugging another wraps around it

parts.note: to tote is to carry or bear
the four letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A cuddly scene: a bear embraces a genuinely shaggy bear.
explanation.walkthrough: Both bears look like animals; the first is the verb to put up with, the last the verb to carry.
explanation.definitionFit: To bear something, such as pain or rudeness, is to put up with or endure it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: American playwright, a person flat on his back?

parts.note: one is used to mean a person, as in one should
someone laid up in bed, unwell

explanation.surface: A dramatist pictured lying flat out.
explanation.walkthrough: Eugene O'Neill wrote Long Day's Journey into Night; the apostrophe is ignored in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Eugene O'Neill was a Nobel-winning dramatist from the United States, author of The Iceman Cometh.

clue.text: Notes, perhaps, written about bachelor in African citadel

indicators.note: something written about another is wrapped around it, placing one inside

parts.note: banknotes are an example of cash
Bachelor of Arts

explanation.surface: Notes written about a single man inside a North African fortress.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Notes' looks like writing or music; the 'perhaps' warns it is money given as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: A casbah is the citadel or old walled quarter of a North African city such as Algiers.

clue.text: Insect starts to chirp: "I'm cricket, and drummer also!"

indicators.note: the starts of words are their first letters, one taken from each

parts.note: the opening letter of each of these six words

explanation.surface: An insect speaks: it chirps like a cricket and drums too.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue also describes the answer: cicadas sing by vibrating drum-like membranes, a near relation of the cricket's chirp.
explanation.definitionFit: The cicada is a large insect famous for the loud shrill song males make.

clue.text: Almost ruined, public transport

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: something bust is broken or ruined

explanation.surface: A grumble that public transport is nearly falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: A bus is a large road vehicle carrying passengers on a route, the commonest form of public transport.

clue.text: Model as concise embodying fifty of David's paintings?

definitions.note: adjectival phrase for the adjective answer

indicators.note: embodying something takes it into the body, placing it inside
to model clay is to reshape it, so these letters are formed into a new shape

parts.note: the nine letters to rearrange
the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: An art critic praising a model's brief portrayal in a painter's works.
explanation.walkthrough: David is Jacques-Louis David, the French painter of The Death of Marat.
explanation.definitionFit: David led French Neoclassicism, whose paintings revived the clean forms and themes of Greek and Roman antiquity.

clue.text: Fungal sacs, somewhat fascinatingly

indicators.note: somewhat means only part of the following word, so the letters lie within it

parts.note: letters two to five of the word

explanation.surface: An enthusiast finds mushroom spore pouches rather fascinating.
explanation.definitionFit: Asci is the plural of ascus, the sac-shaped cell in which certain fungi form their spores.

clue.text: Pretentious litigant doffing cap

indicators.note: doffing a cap takes off what is on top, so in a down clue the first letter goes

parts.note: each side in a lawsuit is a party

explanation.surface: A pompous person in court tips their hat to the judge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doffing cap' looks like courtroom deference but means removing the top letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Arty describes someone showily or affectedly artistic, a sense close to pretentious.

clue.text: Card game, cheat

definitions.meaning: first meaning: short for cribbage, a card game scored on a pegboard
second meaning: to copy someone else's work dishonestly

explanation.walkthrough: Cribbage is a traditional British pub card game, universally called crib.
explanation.definitionFit: Crib is the familiar name for cribbage and also a verb meaning to copy or plagiarise dishonestly.

clue.text: To capacity, lid off, time for the remaining liquid

indicators.note: taking the lid off removes the top, the first letter of the word

parts.note: filled to capacity means full
an age is a long period of time

explanation.surface: Pouring a bottle to the brim, removing its cap, then waiting for what is left.
explanation.walkthrough: Ullage strictly means the space or amount by which a container falls short of full; it is also used for the dregs left in a cask.
explanation.definitionFit: Ullage can mean the sediment or liquid left in a barrel or bottle, the remaining liquid of the definition.

clue.text: Thoroughly unfortunate end, back on newspaper

indicators.note: an unfortunate word has had bad luck, leaving its letters in a sorry jumble
in an across clue, one thing placed on another follows it, so the paper comes first

parts.note: the i is a British daily newspaper
the three letters rearranged
the tail is the back end

explanation.surface: A grim report of an unlucky death written up in the back pages of a paper.
explanation.walkthrough: The i is a British national daily, a sister title of the Independent; 'on' puts the rest after it.
explanation.definitionFit: To do something in detail is to do it thoroughly, covering every particular, an idiom matching the adverb.
